findings.finding: IDC (2026-10-08), Gartner (2026-10-12) and Omdia all put HP's calendar Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) PC shipments at -30.9% YoY to about 10.3-10.4M units. That is the steepest drop of the top vendors (Lenovo -22.6%, Dell -25%). It compares with HP's own Q3 framing of a high-teens H2 unit decline (Q3 printed -16%, which implies roughly -20% in Q4) and with a revenue consensus of $15.35-15.58B (+5 to +6.5% YoY). That consensus requires Personal Systems of about $11.2-11.4B (+8 to +10% on $10.4B), i.e. ASP/mix up about 55% on IDC's units, against +40% in Q3 (PS +18% on units -16%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3 FY26 (2026-08-26) PS revenue beat on price while units fell 16% and PS margin fell to 4.6%. Shares were down about 9% premarket and closed -2.92% on the print. This name has sold its revenue beats when margin or units disappoint.
findings.why_not_priced: The unit data has been public for six weeks and the stock fell about 9% on 2026-10-30, when Intel and IDC framed the slump, so the unit fact itself is partly priced. What looks unpriced is revenue consensus: Chartmill says it was revised UP 7.1% over three months and sits at +5.7% YoY, a number built off Q3's 18% PS beat rather than off a -31% unit quarter. If the market had marked revenue to the unit data, consensus revenue would be near flat YoY (about $14.6-15.0B) rather than $15.4B+.
findings.independence: IDC press release https://idc.com/resource-center/press-releases/idc-pc-tracker-3q26 (2026-10-08) gives the same -30.9%, and Omdia gives about -31% (per the Gartner coverage). Three trackers, one underlying sell-in phenomenon. HP's own PS figures for Q3 are from https://finviz.com/news/385926/hp-inc-reports-fiscal-2026-third-quarter-results. Counterweight: see the Lenovo finding. Price inflation may cover more of the gap than Q3's +40% ASP suggests.

findings.finding: Lenovo, the largest PC vendor, reported on 2026-11-19 for the quarter ended 2026-09-30 (after HP last spoke). Intelligent Devices Group revenue was +15% YoY to a record $17.4B, with double-digit PC revenue growth and an IDG operating margin of 7.1%, 'well maintained', even though IDC had its units at -22.6%. Price/mix more than offset units at the direct peer, which supports HP's PS revenue and margin holding up despite -31% units.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is a peer read-through. HP's own pricing-driven PS beat in Q3 was sold (-2.92%), so price-led revenue has not been paid for on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: It landed five days before HP's print, inside the quarter's blackout. HPQ's 5-day run-up is -0.94%, so the stock has not lifted on it. Lenovo's own share reaction is disputed (TNW/Bloomberg: down more than 5%), so the read-across has not been broadcast as positive.
findings.independence: Lenovo's release is a different document from the IDC/Gartner series. Caveats: IDG includes smartphones (Motorola), HP lost more units than Lenovo (-31% vs -23%), and HP's PS margin (4.6%) already runs well below Lenovo's 7.1%. Reported loss context: https://thenextweb.com/news/lenovo-results-q2-record-revenue-640m-loss-ai-servers

findings.finding: TrendForce (2026-11-11) forecasts PC DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ in 4Q26 after +18-23% in 3Q26. It also reports rising finished-goods inventory at PC OEMs and in North American distribution, notebook shipments -15.8% QoQ in 3Q26 with a further decline in 4Q26, and Korean suppliers planning to cut PC DRAM output by more than 20% YoY in 2027. All of this sits against HP's message that fiscal Q4 is the margin trough and that cheaper inventory is now used up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Nov 2025 the shares slid on a softer FY26 EPS forecast (-1.4% on the print, per the baseline). The Aug 2026 print fell -2.92% on margin and memory-cost commentary despite a beat and raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Memory inflation is the known story, and the skew and run-up partly price it. What is newer is that costs keep rising into HP's FQ1 FY27 (Nov-Jan), together with channel inventory building in North America. If consensus believed the 'Q4 is the trough' line less, the FY27 EPS estimate would not have risen 7.4% over three months (Chartmill).
findings.independence: This is a proxy: industry series, not HP-confirmed. Same-day coverage: https://cryptobriefing.com/trendforce-pc-dram-prices-rise-4q26/ (same TrendForce report, so one source). HP said it has long-term supply agreements covering FY26, which may blunt FQ1 exposure.

findings.finding: HP's 2026-09-21 SEC filing set a planning assumption of a roughly mid-single-digit decline in industry PC units in CY2027 and withheld FY27 guidance until the Q4 print. Several things sit around that: Morgan Stanley (Underweight, $19 target, same day) argues FY27 PS unit declines will exceed 10%; FY26's $3.19-3.29 guide includes $0.19 of tariff refunds that do not recur (an ex-refund base of about $3.05); and consensus FY27 EPS has been revised up about 7.4% over three months. Together these raise the risk that the first FY27 guide lands below the Street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on the next-year guide: the Nov 2025 FY26 guide was soft and the shares slid (sweep cites https://ng.investing.com/news/earnings/hp-inc-shares-slide-after-softer-2026-earnings-forecast-2227859). The baseline shows -1.40% on that print, with -8.27% and -6.82% on guide disappointments in 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell 2-4% on the filing and has since lost 20% from its September high. The tariff-refund non-recurrence is mechanical and the rising FY27 estimate does not obviously net it out. However, the FY27 consensus level could not be sourced, so this is capped small.
findings.independence: Morgan Stanley note: https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/hp-s-unit-and-margin-pressures-not-factored-in-by-the-stock-s-multi-year-valuation-highs-says-morgan-stanley/cZMRjXfRBIc (2026-09-21). The Dow Jones version of the filing is https://www.itiger.com/news/2669157775. Both rest on the same filing for the unit assumption.

findings.finding: HP named former GSK CEO Emma Walmsley as CEO on 2026-11-04, effective 2027-01-04. The FY27 outlook given tonight will therefore be issued by an interim CEO (Bruce Broussard) about six weeks before an outside successor takes over, which raises the odds of a conservative, wide or partial FY27 range.

findings.why_not_priced: The appointment is public, but no preview found connects it to the shape of the FY27 guide; the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-16 still describes the CEO search as ongoing.
